newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: States OK sale of Canberra's National Rail stake.
newsitem.headline: States OK sale of Canberra's National Rail stake.

text.p: The Australian federal government's sale of 72.8 percent stake in freight operator National Rail moved a step closer on Monday as federal ministers said the other shareholders, two states, had approved the sale.

The federal Office of Asset Sales had commisssioned LEK Partnership, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and lawyers Blake Dawson Waldron to study options for the sale, Finance Minister John Fahey and Transport Minister John Sharp said in a statement.
That study would take five weeks, after which the government would detail a timetable for the sale of its stake.
"The current study, the first step in the sales process, could not commence without the agreement of all the other shareholders," the ministers said.
They said the other shareholders, the states of New South Wales and Victoria, would be consulted fully throughout the study.

The federal government announced its intention to sell National Rail last November. It has also put the wholly-owned Australian National rail operator up for sale with final bids expected at the end of July.
Australian National operates freight services and workshops in South Australia and Tasmania, in addition to three interstate passenger services.
Analysts expect its sale to raise up to A$600 million.
